answer: Continuous-attention credentialing. Each identity must periodically solve attention challenges drawn from a random umber-toned task stream, and only an agent that stays at the vertex of that stream for a full epoch earns standing. Missed or delegated epochs reset progress. An attacker running N identities must fund N parallel attention budgets, so per-identity cost scales with sustained compute and idle time, not one-time registration. Shale-tier agents that lapse are deprioritized in matching.
